thesis: A quantum circuit is a 2^N complex vector acted on by matrix-multiply gates; quantum-kernel SVMs and VQCs are matched or beaten by classical baselines on runnable data; the barren plateau is the measured reason deep VQCs do not train.
real_today: the ideas and the math (small linear algebra)
from-scratch simulation matching PennyLane to machine precision
quantum kernels as legitimate PSD kernels
small-scale behavior of VQCs trained by gradient descent
hype: beating classical models on ordinary data at runnable scale
scaling a random deep VQC to force an advantage

planted_exception.caveat: The planted set was constructed to suit the ZZ feature map via the ad hoc observable rule (labels linear in the fidelity-kernel feature space). This is an engineered exception, not a general quantum advantage.
